---
name: flutter-install-does-not-rebuild
description: "Deploying flux-app to a device — `flutter install` does NOT rebuild; build first or you ship a stale APK"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: d4342d71-403d-4ea0-921d-f3351ebb9556
---

`flutter install` does **NOT** compile — it only pushes the existing
`build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-release.apk`. After editing any Dart/Kotlin
in flux-app, `flutter install` silently installs a **stale cached APK**, so your
changes never reach the device.

**Why:** this wasted several debug cycles — "the fix isn't working" when the fix
was never actually on the phone (the installed APK was from a previous day).

**How to apply — to deploy a change to the Pixel 6 (`24221FDF6005YN`):**
1. Build from source: `flutter build apk --release` (or `flutter run --release` to build+install+attach). This actually recompiles.
2. Then install the fresh APK: `flutter install -d 24221FDF6005YN` **or** `adb -s 24221FDF6005YN install -r build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-release.apk`.
3. **Verify** before testing: `stat -c '%y' build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-release.apk` must be newer than the edited sources. If a fix "doesn't work," check this first.

Note: release builds strip `debugPrint`, so Dart `I/E flutter:` logs won't show in logcat; native Kotlin `Log.*` (e.g. `CommissioningBridge`) still do. Use `flutter run` / a debug build when you need Dart logs.

Same trap exists on the controller side: code changes don't take effect until the user **flashes** flux-controller. See [[flux-thread-br-commissioning]].

The fresh APK is built (85.8 MB, timestamped just now). The only blocker is the **adb connection** — the host is reachable and port 37119 is open, but `adb connect` is rejected. On Android 11+ wireless debugging this means this machine isn't **paired** with the device yet, which needs a separate pairing port + 6-digit code that I can't get on my own.

To pair, on the phone go to **Settings → Developer options → Wireless debugging → Pair device with pairing code**. That shows an `IP:PORT` and a 6-digit code (the pairing port is different from 37119). Then run this yourself in the prompt:

```
! adb pair 192.168.1.179:<pairing-port> <code>
```

Once paired, I'll `adb connect 192.168.1.179:37119` and install the APK.
